Memory as Architecture

How neural design shapes remembering

The way we process and perceive memories is also a consequence of how our brains operate at a neural-network level i.e. physical architecture.

Memory is not a “file” saved somewhere; it is an emergent state of physical neural networks. The evolved architecture of the hippocampus–neocortex system, synaptic plasticity rules, and large-scale dynamics (sleep, oscillations) together produce selective, reconstructive, and adaptive memory.
